sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42404 2 CRA-9290-2024 2.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that, even as per the prosecution story, it is a case of non-penetrative sexual assault as bas been proved by Dr. Preetika Singh (PW-8).
It is further submitted that, it is a case of false accusation and the victim is tried to settle her personal score with the appellant.
In fact, appellant was beaten by her father as he was trying to control the crowed of the Government Hospital and a counter blast report has been lodged.

3. Shri Manasmani Verma, learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State submits that it is not a simple case of counter blast but as far as evidence of prosecutrix (PW-1) that the appellant in the name of dental checkup had violate privacy of the victim, but Dr. Preetika Singh (PW-8) has not opined about any penetrative sexual assault.
Appellant's case will fall under Section 7 of the POCSO Act and accordingly, the impugned judgment of conviction can be suitably modified.
4. After, hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the records.
5. Victim (PW-1) admitted that immediately after the incident, she had not given any intimation to her father in the hospital.
She admitted that, after the incident, she had not given any intimation to any of the Doctors or the Staff.
On the date of incident, she had reported this matter to her mother a t 0 8 : 0 0 p . m .
S h e a d m i t t e d t h a t , s h e h a d r e a c h e d N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O

. 
2025:MPHC-JBP:42404 3 CRA-9290-2024 her home at about 04-04:30 p.m.
She admitted that, no bleeding took place due to the act of the appellant nor any injury was sustained by her.
She admitted that, the incident took place inside the chamber of the Doctor.
She also admitted that, except for her and her family members, nobody else have information about the incident.
She also admitted that the chamber in which examination was allegedly conducted is visible from outside.
She admitted that, in Ex.P-3, he had pressed her private part, is mentioned whereas, in the Court statements she stated that appellant had inserted his finger in her private part.
6. Thus, there is contradiction in the statements of the victim.
Dr. Preetika Singh (PW-8) has categorically stated that, there were no injury marks and there were no symptoms of any sexual violence against the appellant.

7. When, these facts are taken into consideration, even if the testimony of the prosecutrix is believe to be correct then, at best it would be a case which falls under the category of not penetrative sexual assault as defined under Section 7 of the POCSO Act punishable under Section 8 of POCSO Act.

8. Accordingly, impugned judgment dated 20.07.2024 passed in S.C. No. 23 of 2022 is modified and conviction is altered from one under Section 376(3) of IPC and under Section 4 & 6 of POCSO Act to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for 20 years, 10 years and 10 years with NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:42404 4 CRA-9290-2024 fine of Rs.10,000/-, Rs.10,000/- & Rs. 10,000/-
respectively with default stipulations to one under Sections 7/8 of the POCSO Act and appellant is directed to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for a period of 04 years and fine of Rs.2000/- with default stipulation of Rigorous Imprisonment for one month.
